chains.title: FOXA1-bound enhancer: alt T increases FOXA1 binding and TOX3 expression
chains.cell_type: MCF-7 / ER-positive luminal breast cancer cells

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies this element in MCF-7 (E05); the alt T allele is predicted to bind FOXA1 more strongly than ref C. FOXA1 is selected because it is a pioneer TF with MCF-7 ChIP peaks containing the variant (E05), high MCF-7 expression (E05), the variant lies in a dELS (E03), and E19 includes PMID 23001124 reporting that breast cancer risk SNPs modulate FOXA1 chromatin affinity and gene expression. No QBiC-SELEX model for FOXA1 is supplied, and the exact allele direction at this base is not measured in the provided evidence; bulk ChIP cannot prove allelic imbalance.

The variant lies in ENSR16_9QTBS and in cCRE EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like element, and FOXA1 ChIP peaks containing the variant place FOXA1 at this element in MCF-7; this supports a FOXA1-bound distal enhancer-like element in the relevant cell type, though the cCRE z-scores are maxima across biosamples.

TOX3 is the best-nominated target because it is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb upstream (E02), Open Targets L2G gives TOX3 the top score in breast cancer credible sets (E16), and E18a links rs4784227/TOX3 as an enhancer example; however, direct regulatory linkage is not established because GTEx v8 shows no significant single-tissue or breast eQTL for this exact variant (E17, E20), and TOX3 is not essential in MCF7 or breast lineage lines by DepMap (E21), so this is target nomination rather than demonstrated rs4784227-to-TOX3 regulation.

MCF-7 is a relevant ER-positive luminal breast cancer context: FOXA1 ChIP-seq is present in MCF-7 at this element (E05), FOXA1 is highly expressed there (E05), the expression context is DepMap:ACH-000019 (MCF7), and the GWAS signal is strong for breast cancer including ER-positive disease (E15, E16).

The alt T allele is the breast cancer risk allele in the strongest GWAS and meta-analysis evidence (T vs C OR about 1.24; E15, E18b), and one E15 entry reports effect allele C, likely reflecting effect-allele coding inconsistency rather than contradicting the T-risk direction. If alt T increases FOXA1-bound enhancer activity and TOX3 expression, this would be expected to raise risk, especially ER-positive breast cancer, but the causal steps from FOXA1 binding to TOX3 expression to disease are inferential, and TOX3 perturbation does not affect MCF7 fitness in DepMap (E21).

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 binding assays show alt T > ref C at this base.
An enhancer reporter carrying alt T has higher activity than ref C in MCF-7 cells.
TOX3 expression is higher with the T allele in an appropriate ER-positive breast context.
FOXA1 knockdown or CRISPRi reduces TOX3 expression in MCF-7 cells.
CRISPRi or deletion of this dELS lowers TOX3 expression in MCF-7 cells.
falsified_if: FOXA1 binding is not allele-specific at this base.
Ref C binds FOXA1 more strongly than alt T.
The T allele does not change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity.
Direct perturbation of the element does not affect TOX3.

TOX3 is not essential in MCF7 or breast lineage lines by DepMap (E21), so the disease mechanism may not require a strong TOX3 expression change.

links.claim: GATA3 occupies this element in MCF-7 (E06); the alt T allele is predicted to bind GATA3 more strongly than ref C. GATA3 is extremely highly expressed in MCF-7 (rank 5 of 1626 TFs; E06) and has MCF-7 ChIP peaks containing the variant, but E04 shows many other bound, expressed TFs and no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data for GATA3 are supplied, so the allelic direction is a hypothesis rather than a measured effect.
The variant lies in the dELS EH38E3180851 (E03), and GATA3 ChIP peaks containing the variant place GATA3 at this enhancer-like element in MCF-7 (E06).

TOX3 is the best-nominated target because it is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb upstream (E02), Open Targets L2G gives TOX3 the top score in breast cancer credible sets (E16), and E18a links rs4784227/TOX3 as an enhancer example; however, direct regulatory linkage is not established because GTEx v8 shows no significant single-tissue or breast eQTL for this exact variant (E17, E20), and TOX3 is not essential in MCF7 or breast lineage lines by DepMap (E21), so this is target nomination rather than demonstrated rs4784227-to-TOX3 regulation.

MCF-7 is a relevant ER-positive luminal breast cancer context: GATA3 is very highly expressed and bound at this element in MCF-7 (E06), and the GWAS signal is strong for breast cancer including ER-positive disease (E15, E16).

The alt T allele is associated with increased breast cancer risk (E15, E18b); if alt T increases GATA3-bound enhancer activity and TOX3 expression, this could increase risk in ER-positive breast cancer, but whether GATA3 binding at this element increases TOX3 and whether that changes risk is not directly shown, and TOX3 perturbation does not affect MCF7 fitness in DepMap (E21).

GATA3 knockdown does not affect TOX3 expression.
The element's activity is FOXA1-dependent but GATA3-independent.

grades_v0.reason: FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF-7 contain the variant (E05), so occupancy is supported. However, no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding assay is supplied, and the claim that alt T binds FOXA1 more strongly than ref C is explicitly a hypothesis, not measured. Bulk ChIP cannot distinguish alleles.

E01 places the variant in ENSR16_9QTBS, E03 places it in the dELS EH38E3180851, and E05 shows FOXA1 ChIP peaks containing the variant in MCF-7. This supports a FOXA1-bound distal enhancer-like element in the relevant cell type, though the cCRE z-scores are maxima across biosamples rather than MCF-7-specific.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene (E02) and Open Targets L2G nominates TOX3 strongly (E16), and E18a links rs4784227/TOX3 as an enhancer example. But E17 reports no significant GTEx v8 single-tissue eQTL, the TOX3 eQTL credible sets in E16 have low PIP, and no enhancer-promoter contact or perturbation is shown. This supports target nomination, not a demonstrated rs4784227-to-TOX3 expression link.

MCF-7 is explicitly the expression context, FOXA1 ChIP-seq is present in MCF-7 at this element (E05), FOXA1 is highly expressed there, and the GWAS signal is strong for breast cancer including ER-positive disease (E15, E16).

The alt T allele is strongly supported as the breast cancer risk allele by GWAS and meta-analysis (E15, E18b), and the hypothesized direction (alt T increases FOXA1 binding/enhancer activity/TOX3, increasing risk) is internally consistent. But the causal steps from increased FOXA1 binding to increased TOX3 expression to increased breast cancer risk are not directly shown.

GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF-7 contain the variant (E06), so occupancy is supported. No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data are supplied, so the claim that alt T binds GATA3 more strongly is a hypothesis. GATA3 is highly expressed and plausible, but selection among many bound TFs is not discriminative.
E03 identifies the variant in dELS EH38E3180851, and E06 shows GATA3 ChIP peaks containing the variant in MCF-7. This supports GATA3 occupancy at an enhancer-like element in the relevant cell type.

Same issue as H1.gene: TOX3 is nearest and strongly nominated by L2G (E02, E16), and E18a gives a review-level TOX3 link, but there is no eQTL (E17 null), no contact, and no perturbation showing rs4784227 regulates TOX3. This is target nomination rather than direct regulatory evidence.
GATA3 is bound at this element and very highly expressed in MCF-7 (E06), and the disease context includes ER-positive breast cancer (E15, E16).

The T allele is supported as risk-increasing (E15, E18b). However, whether GATA3 binding at this element increases TOX3 and whether that increases breast cancer risk is not shown; GATA3 can be context-dependent, and no functional perturbation is cited.

SPDEF ChIP-seq peaks in MCF-7 contain the variant (E07), so occupancy is supported. The claim that ref C binds SPDEF more strongly than alt T is not measured; there is no QBiC-SELEX, motif change, or allele-specific assay. SPDEF is also chosen among many bound TFs without an allelic rationale.
E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E3180851 and E07 shows SPDEF ChIP peaks containing the variant in MCF-7, supporting SPDEF occupancy at this enhancer-like element.

TOX3 is nearest and L2G-nominated (E02, E16), but the regulatory link is not directly demonstrated; E17 is null for GTEx v8 eQTLs and no contact/perturbation is cited. The gene link is independent of SPDEF and remains a target nomination.
SPDEF is expressed in MCF-7 and bound at this element (E07), and MCF-7/ER-positive breast cancer is a relevant disease context (E15, E16).

The T allele is supported as the risk allele (E15, E18b), but the repression-loss model requires that SPDEF normally represses TOX3 and that weaker SPDEF binding on alt T increases TOX3. No cited evidence shows SPDEF represses TOX3 at this element or anywhere relevant; this arm is effectively unsupported.

NR2F2 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF-7 contain the variant (E08), so occupancy is supported. The claim that ref C binds NR2F2 more strongly than alt T is not measured; no QBiC-SELEX, motif change, or allele-specific assay is provided. NR2F2 is one of many bound TFs with no allelic prioritization.
E03 identifies the variant in dELS EH38E3180851 and E08 shows NR2F2 ChIP peaks containing the variant in MCF-7, supporting NR2F2 occupancy at this enhancer-like element.

TOX3 is nearest and strongly L2G-nominated (E02, E16), but no eQTL/contact/perturbation directly connects rs4784227 to TOX3 expression; E17 is null. The gene link is a target nomination, not demonstrated regulation.
NR2F2 is expressed in MCF-7 and bound at this element (E08), and ER-positive breast cancer is a relevant GWAS context (E15, E16).

The T allele is supported as risk-increasing (E15, E18b), but the NR2F2 repression-loss model is speculative: no cited evidence shows NR2F2 represses TOX3 at this element, and the direction from weaker NR2F2 binding to higher TOX3 to higher risk is not tested.

grades_final.reason: FOXA1 occupancy at the variant in MCF-7 is supported by E05 ChIP peaks and expression, but the alt-T-binds-more direction is not measured. No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding assay is supplied; E19 is only a generic literature title and does not specify rs4784227 or an allele direction. Bulk ChIP cannot establish allelic imbalance.

E01 places the variant in ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer, E03 places it in dELS EH38E3180851, and E05 provides MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP peaks containing the variant. This directly supports a FOXA1-bound distal enhancer-like element in the relevant cell type. The cCRE z-score caveat does not undermine the element identity.

E02 proximity and E16 L2G support TOX3 as the best-nominated target, and E18a repeats the rs4784227-TOX3 association, but E17 and E20 show no significant GTEx eQTL and no perturbation demonstrates that rs4784227 regulates TOX3. The claim itself correctly limits this to target nomination rather than demonstrated regulation.

MCF-7 is the supplied expression context, and E05 directly shows FOXA1 ChIP occupancy and high FOXA1 expression there. E15 and E16 support breast cancer and ER-positive disease relevance. This is adequate support for MCF-7 as a relevant breast cancer cell context.

E15 and E18b directly support alt T as the breast cancer risk allele, with T-vs-C OR about 1.24 in the meta-analysis and strong breast cancer GWAS associations. The direction is consistent with the proposed alt-T-increasing model. The FOXA1-to-TOX3-to-risk causal step remains inferential, but the variant-phenotype association link itself is supported.

GATA3 occupancy at the variant in MCF-7 is supported by E06 ChIP peaks and high expression, but the alt-T-binds-more direction is not measured. No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding assay is supplied, and E04 shows many other bound expressed TFs, so GATA3 allele-specific selection is not established.

E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E3180851, and E06 provides MCF-7 GATA3 ChIP peaks containing the variant. This directly supports GATA3 occupancy at this distal enhancer-like element in the relevant cell type.

E02 proximity and E16 L2G support TOX3 as the best-nominated target, and E18a repeats the rs4784227-TOX3 association, but E17 and E20 show no significant GTEx eQTL and no perturbation demonstrates that rs4784227 regulates TOX3. The claim itself limits this to target nomination rather than demonstrated regulation.

MCF-7 is the supplied expression context, and E06 directly shows GATA3 ChIP occupancy and very high GATA3 expression there. E15 and E16 support breast cancer and ER-positive disease relevance. This is adequate support for MCF-7 as a relevant breast cancer cell context.

E15 and E18b directly support alt T as the breast cancer risk allele, with strong GWAS and meta-analysis evidence. The direction is consistent with the proposed alt-T-increasing model. The GATA3-to-TOX3-to-risk causal step remains inferential, but the variant-phenotype association link itself is supported.

checks.args_json: {"query":"rs4784227 allele-specific FOXA1 GATA3 TOX3 enhancer reporter"}
checks.why: This is the most direct way to find published allele-specific binding or reporter assays at this exact base, which would determine whether the FOXA1/GATA3 alt>ref hypotheses have any measured support.
A breast-specific eQTL for this variant would directly test the TOX3 expression link and would substantially raise or lower all TOX3-targeting chains.

DepMap CRISPR knockout effects in breast cancer lineage would test whether TOX3 perturbation is functionally relevant to breast cancer cell fitness, informing the phenotype arm that currently relies on genetic association alone.
